modelResponse.episodeSummary: Patricia L. Harmon, 64F, presents with critical atrial flutter, hemodynamically unstable (hypotensive)
modelResponse.primaryEtiology: Flecainide-induced atrial flutter with rapid ventricular response due to 1:1 AV conduction
modelResponse.mechanism: Class Ic antiarrhythmic (flecainide) can slow atrial conduction, potentially promoting the development of atrial flutter, and can also facilitate 1:1 AV conduction, especially in the absence of an AV nodal blocker.
contributingFactors: Patient history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
Recent initiation of flecainide (2 weeks ago) without concomitant AV nodal blocking agent

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Ischemic heart disease causing atrial flutter
rejectedAlternatives.why: No significant ST deviation reported (obscured by wide QRS), troponin T is only mildly elevated (likely demand ischemia given presentation and recent activity), no history of structural heart disease.
Potassium is normal (4.1 mmol/L), Magnesium is normal (2.0 mg/dL). No other electrolyte data provided.

recommendedActions: Immediate synchronized cardioversion (due to hemodynamic instability: MAP 65 mmHg, lightheadedness)
Administer IV fluids (e.g., 250-500 mL bolus) for hypotension
Consider IV beta-blocker (e.g., metoprolol) or calcium channel blocker (e.g., diltiazem) *after* cardioversion if flutter recurs, but only if hemodynamically stable and no contraindications
Monitor potassium and magnesium levels closely
uncertainty: Exact morphology of flutter waves is difficult to assess due to wide QRS
Underlying cause of mild troponin elevation is unclear (likely demand ischemia)
